title: Payments API Reference v3
text: The Payments API exposes REST endpoints to create, capture and refund transactions. All requests require an OAuth2 bearer token in the Authorization header. Responses are returned in JSON and errors follow the RFC 7807 problem format. Rate limits are 100 requests per second per client.

title: Microservices Architecture Overview
text: This document describes the microservices architecture of the retail platform. Each service owns its database and communicates through an event bus using Kafka topics. The API gateway handles routing, authentication and request throttling. Services are deployed as Docker containers on Kubernetes.

title: Kubernetes Deployment Guide
text: Follow these steps to deploy a service to the Kubernetes cluster. Build the Docker image, push it to the container registry and update the Helm chart values. Run helm upgrade with the staging namespace and verify the pods are healthy with kubectl get pods.

title: Database Schema for Inventory Service
text: The inventory service uses PostgreSQL with three main tables: products, warehouses and stock_movements. Foreign keys enforce referential integrity and an index on product_id speeds up stock queries. Schema migrations are managed with Flyway and versioned in the repository.

title: CI/CD Pipeline Configuration
text: The continuous integration pipeline runs on GitHub Actions. Every pull request triggers unit tests, static code analysis with SonarQube and a container build. Merges to the main branch automatically deploy to staging, and production releases require a tagged version.

title: Authentication Module Design
text: The authentication module implements OpenID Connect with an external identity provider. Access tokens expire after fifteen minutes and refresh tokens after seven days. The module validates JWT signatures using the provider public keys cached in Redis.

title: Logging and Monitoring Setup
text: Applications write structured JSON logs that are shipped to Elasticsearch through Fluent Bit. Metrics are exposed in Prometheus format and visualized in Grafana dashboards. Alert rules notify the on-call channel when latency or error rate exceed thresholds.

title: Mobile App Technical Specification
text: The mobile application is built with React Native and shares business logic with the web client. Offline data is stored in SQLite and synchronized through the sync API endpoint. Push notifications are delivered through Firebase Cloud Messaging.

title: API Versioning Standard
text: Public APIs must include the major version in the URL path, for example /v2/orders. Breaking changes require a new major version and the previous version is supported for twelve months. Endpoints document request parameters, response schemas and error codes in OpenAPI.

title: Caching Strategy for Product Catalog
text: The product catalog uses a read-through cache in Redis with a time to live of ten minutes. Cache keys include the store identifier and the locale. When a product is updated an event invalidates the related keys to avoid stale data.

title: Terraform Infrastructure Modules
text: Cloud infrastructure is defined as code using Terraform modules for networking, databases and compute. Each environment has its own state file stored in a remote backend with locking. Variables configure instance sizes, subnets and security groups.

title: Message Queue Integration Guide
text: Producers publish order events to the RabbitMQ exchange using a routing key per event type. Consumers must acknowledge messages after processing and failed messages are sent to a dead letter queue. Payloads are serialized with Avro schemas registered in the schema registry.

title: Information Security Policy
text: All employees must protect company and client information according to this policy. Passwords must have at least twelve characters and multi-factor authentication is mandatory. Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action up to termination of employment.

title: Remote Work Policy
text: Employees may work remotely up to three days per week with approval from their manager. Remote workers must use the company VPN and keep confidential documents secure at home. Core collaboration hours are from 10:00 to 15:00 local time.

title: Travel and Expense Reimbursement Procedure
text: Business travel must be approved in advance by the department manager. Employees submit expense reports with original receipts within fifteen days after the trip. Meals are reimbursed up to the daily allowance and alcohol is not reimbursable.

title: Data Privacy and Personal Data Protection Policy
text: Personal data of clients and employees is processed only for legitimate purposes and with consent. Access to personal data is restricted by role and every request from a data subject must be answered within twenty days. The data protection officer supervises compliance with this policy.

title: Code of Conduct
text: Softtek expects all employees to act with integrity, respect and professionalism. Harassment, discrimination and conflicts of interest are strictly prohibited. Employees must report suspected violations to the ethics committee through the confidential reporting channel.

title: Acceptable Use of IT Resources
text: Company laptops, email and software licenses are provided for business purposes. Installing unauthorized software or sharing credentials is prohibited. The IT department may monitor the use of company resources to ensure compliance with this policy.

title: Change Management Procedure
text: Every change to production systems requires a change request approved by the change advisory board. The request must describe the risk, the rollback plan and the maintenance window. Emergency changes can be approved by the duty manager and reviewed afterwards.

title: Vacation and Leave Policy
text: Employees are entitled to vacation days according to their seniority and local labor law. Leave requests must be submitted through the HR portal at least two weeks in advance. Managers approve requests considering project deadlines and team coverage.

title: Access Control Procedure
text: Access to systems is granted according to the principle of least privilege. Managers request access through the service desk and the security team approves it. Access rights are reviewed every quarter and revoked immediately when an employee leaves the company.

title: Document Retention Policy
text: Contracts, invoices and project records must be retained for at least five years. Documents that exceed the retention period are securely destroyed following the disposal procedure. Legal holds suspend destruction when litigation is expected.

title: Procurement and Vendor Selection Procedure
text: Purchases above five thousand dollars require three vendor quotations and approval from finance. Vendors must sign the confidentiality agreement and pass the security assessment. The procurement team keeps a register of approved suppliers.

title: Business Continuity Policy
text: The company maintains a business continuity plan to keep critical services operating during disruptions. Each department must identify critical processes and recovery time objectives. The plan is tested once a year and approved by the executive committee.

title: Retail Platform Project Status Report - March
text: The retail platform project is on schedule and eighty percent of the planned features are complete. The budget consumption is at sixty five percent. The main risk is the delay of the payment provider integration, which may affect the go-live milestone in June.

title: Sprint 14 Review - Logistics App
text: During sprint 14 the team delivered the route optimization feature and fixed twelve bugs. Velocity was 42 story points, above the average of the last three sprints. The client approved the demo and requested changes to the delivery tracking screen.

title: Lessons Learned - Banking Portal Project
text: The banking portal project finished two weeks late and five percent over budget. The main lesson learned is to involve the client security team from the first phase. Automated testing reduced regression defects and should be adopted in future projects.

title: Quarterly Portfolio Report Q2
text: In the second quarter the company managed fourteen active client projects. Eleven projects are green, two are yellow and one is red due to scope changes. Customer satisfaction averaged 4.5 out of 5 and revenue grew twelve percent.

title: Cloud Migration Project Closure Report
text: The cloud migration project moved forty applications from the client data center to the cloud. The project closed within budget and infrastructure costs were reduced by thirty percent. Pending items were handed over to the operations team.

title: Project Kickoff Minutes - Insurance CRM
text: The kickoff meeting defined the project scope, the stakeholders and the communication plan. The project manager presented the timeline with four milestones and the risk register. The client sponsor approved the project charter.

title: Risk Assessment - E-commerce Redesign
text: The project team identified seven risks for the e-commerce redesign. The highest risk is the dependency on the client content team for product images. Mitigation actions and owners were assigned and the risk register will be reviewed weekly.

title: Weekly Status Report - Data Warehouse
text: This week the team completed the ingestion pipelines for sales and inventory data. Two milestones were reached and one task is blocked waiting for database credentials from the client. The schedule variance is three days and the forecast remains on track.

title: Client Satisfaction Survey Results - Logistics
text: The client rated the project team 4.7 out of 5 in communication and 4.2 in delivery speed. Comments highlight the quality of the deliverables and request more frequent progress reports. Action items were added to the project plan.

title: Budget Variance Report - Mobile Banking
text: Actual costs of the mobile banking project exceed the baseline budget by eight percent. The variance is caused by additional effort on regulatory requirements. The project manager requests a change order to the client to cover the extra scope.

title: Sprint 22 Retrospective - Payments Team
text: The team agreed that code reviews were faster this sprint but story estimation was inaccurate. Action items include refining the backlog before planning and limiting work in progress. Team morale improved after the successful release.

title: Executive Summary - Digital Transformation Roadmap
text: The roadmap project delivered an assessment of the client current capabilities and a three year transformation plan. Twelve initiatives were prioritized by value and effort. The steering committee approved phase one with a budget of two million dollars.

title: New Employee Onboarding Guide
text: Welcome to Softtek. During your first week you will set up your laptop, complete the mandatory courses and meet your mentor. This guide explains how to request access to tools, where to find documentation and who to contact for help.

title: Git Fundamentals Course
text: In this course you will learn how to clone a repository, create branches and commit changes. Lesson two explains merging and resolving conflicts. At the end of each lesson complete the practice exercise and the quiz to earn the certificate.

title: Introduction to Kubernetes Training
text: This training module introduces containers, pods, services and deployments. Learners follow a step by step lab to deploy a sample application. The module includes a final assessment and recommended reading for the certification exam.

title: Secure Coding Workshop Manual
text: This workshop teaches developers how to prevent common vulnerabilities such as SQL injection and cross site scripting. Participants practice with hands-on exercises in a vulnerable sample application. Completion of the workshop is required for all developers each year.

title: Agile and Scrum Training for Consultants
text: Learn the Scrum roles, events and artifacts through practical examples. The course explains how to write user stories, estimate with story points and run a sprint retrospective. Each module ends with a short quiz to check your understanding.

title: Customer Communication Skills Course
text: This course helps consultants communicate effectively with clients. Lessons cover active listening, writing clear emails and presenting technical results to non technical audiences. Learners complete role play exercises with feedback from the instructor.

title: How to Use the Knowledge Base
text: This tutorial explains how to search, read and contribute articles in the company knowledge base. Learn how to tag documents, use templates and request a review from a subject matter expert. Screenshots guide you through each step.

title: Python for Data Analysis Course
text: The course introduces Python, pandas and data visualization for analysts. Students learn to load datasets, clean data and create charts. Each lesson includes a notebook with exercises and the solutions are reviewed in the final session.

title: Cloud Practitioner Learning Path
text: This learning path prepares employees for the cloud practitioner certification. It contains video lessons on cloud concepts, pricing and security, followed by practice exams. Learners who pass the exam receive a voucher reimbursement.

title: Leadership Program for Team Leads
text: The leadership program develops skills to coach team members, give feedback and manage conflicts. Participants attend four workshops and complete a personal development plan. A mentor follows each participant during the program.

title: Testing Best Practices Tutorial
text: This tutorial teaches how to write unit tests, integration tests and end to end tests. Learners practice test driven development with guided exercises. The tutorial includes examples in Java and JavaScript and a checklist for code reviews.

title: Information Security Awareness Training
text: This mandatory training teaches employees to recognize phishing emails and protect their passwords. The course contains short videos, real examples and a final quiz. Employees must complete the training every year to keep their system access.

title: Post-mortem: Payments API Outage
text: On May 3 the Payments API was unavailable for 47 minutes. The root cause was an expired TLS certificate on the load balancer. Customers could not complete purchases during the outage. Corrective actions include automatic certificate renewal and an expiration alert.

title: Security Incident: Phishing Campaign
text: Several employees received a phishing email impersonating the HR portal. Two users entered their credentials before the security team blocked the domain. Passwords were reset, sessions revoked and no data exfiltration was detected.

title: Root Cause Analysis: Database Performance Degradation
text: Response times of the inventory service increased tenfold during the peak hour. The root cause analysis found a missing index after a schema migration. The index was restored and a performance test was added to the release checklist.

title: Incident Report: Data Center Network Failure
text: A failure in the core switch caused a network outage affecting internal applications for two hours. The operations team activated the backup link and escalated to the vendor. The faulty hardware was replaced and the incident was closed.

title: Post-mortem: Failed Production Deployment
text: A deployment introduced a configuration error that caused errors in the checkout service. The on-call engineer detected the alert and performed a rollback after twenty minutes. Impact was limited to three percent of transactions. Action items include a configuration validation step.

title: Incident: Unauthorized Access Attempt
text: The intrusion detection system flagged repeated failed login attempts from an unknown IP address. The account was locked and the IP was blocked at the firewall. Investigation confirmed that no access was obtained and the incident severity was set to medium.

title: Post-mortem: Message Queue Backlog
text: Order events accumulated in the queue and were processed with a delay of three hours. The root cause was a consumer that crashed due to an unhandled malformed message. A fix was deployed and monitoring of queue depth was added to the alerts.

title: Incident Report: Mobile App Crash After Release
text: After release 5.2 the mobile app crashed on startup for Android 10 users. The crash rate reached twelve percent within two hours. A hotfix was published and the release process now includes testing on older devices.

title: Incident: Accidental Data Exposure
text: A storage bucket with test data was configured as public by mistake. The exposure was detected by the cloud security scanner after six hours. The bucket was made private, access logs were reviewed and the data protection officer was notified.

title: Post-mortem: Cache Stampede on Product Catalog
text: When the cache cluster restarted all requests went to the database at the same time, causing timeouts. The service was degraded for thirty minutes. Corrective actions include request coalescing and staggered cache expiration.

title: Incident Report: Third-Party Email Service Outage
text: The external email provider suffered an outage and order confirmation emails were not sent for four hours. Messages were queued and delivered when the service recovered. A secondary provider will be configured for failover.

title: Root Cause Analysis: Disk Full on Logging Server
text: The logging server ran out of disk space and stopped accepting logs. The alert threshold was misconfigured and the issue was detected late. Log rotation was fixed, old indices were deleted and disk usage alerts were corrected.
